about.text: Estimator: how many doors and windows of each type sit on each storey of the Duplex, and what size are they? Sizes are the IFC OverallWidth and OverallHeight of each door and window (metres in the model, shown in millimetres); Area_m2 is width times height per opening, summed per schedule line. A schedule line is one storey, kind, type, and size, so a type with two sizes would show as two lines; an opening with no size keeps an empty size and area, never zero. Result: 38 openings on 11 lines. Doors: 14 (Level 1: two 762 x 2032, two 813 x 2420, two 1250 x 2010; Level 2: two 762 x 2032, six 864 x 2032). Windows: 24 (Level 1: two 4835 x 2420, two 750 x 2200; Level 2: four 2800 x 2410, two 750 x 2200, twelve 819 x 759; Roof: two skylights). Check before pricing the skylights: their type is named 1180 x 1170mm but the IFC gives 1173 x 635 mm, while Revit's own Height parameter says 1170, so the IFC height looks like a sloped or projected dimension. Reading the figure: one bar per schedule line, its length the count, coloured by opening type; the Vega-Lite spec groups the bars by storey. The 3D view uses the same colours for the same types and fades everything that is not a door or window to 15 percent. The eighth type in sorted order (Window 750mm x 2200mm) takes category10's grey, close to the grey of uncoloured elements; in 3D it stays opaque while those fade.

openings.sql: SELECT e.EntityIndex, e.StepId, e.GlobalId, CASE e.Category WHEN 'IFCDOOR' THEN 'Door' ELSE 'Window' END AS Kind, e.Type, s.StoreyName AS Storey FROM EntityText e LEFT JOIN StoreyOfElement s ON s.EntityIndex = e.EntityIndex AND s.Depth = 1 WHERE e.Category IN ('IFCDOOR', 'IFCWINDOW') ORDER BY e.StepId

sizes.sql: SELECT p.EntityIndex, round(max(CASE WHEN p.Name = 'Ifc:OverallWidth' THEN TRY_CAST(p.Value AS DOUBLE) END) * 1000) AS Width_mm, round(max(CASE WHEN p.Name = 'Ifc:OverallHeight' THEN TRY_CAST(p.Value AS DOUBLE) END) * 1000) AS Height_mm FROM ParameterText p JOIN EntityText e ON e.EntityIndex = p.EntityIndex WHERE e.Category IN ('IFCDOOR', 'IFCWINDOW') AND p.Name IN ('Ifc:OverallWidth', 'Ifc:OverallHeight') GROUP BY p.EntityIndex

schedule.groupBy: Storey, Kind, Type, OpeningType, Width_mm, Height_mm
schedule.aggregates: count(*) as Count, sum(Area_m2) as Area_m2

scheduleTable.title: Opening schedule per storey
scheduleTable.columns: Storey, Kind, Type, Width_mm, Height_mm, Count, Area_m2
